source.title: Fair Division under Joint Ownership: Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: In the manna-division problem, where a fixed stock of unproduced goods is divided among agents with arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences, does there exist a Pareto optimal mechanism that satisfies Population Monotonicity and No Domination, where Population Monotonicity means that when an additional agent joins the population sharing the same cake no pre-existing agent benefits, and No Domination means that no agent ever receives a strictly bigger share of every good than another agent? If such a mechanism exists, can one also require Equal Split Guarantee, meaning that each agent's welfare is at least as high as the welfare of that agent's per-capita share of the resources?
accepted.context_brief: Manna division with fairness and monotonicity constraints

evidence.quote: Question 1. Manna Division. Say that a mechanism satisfies No Domination (Moulin and Thomson 1988) if it never gives to an agent a strictly bigger share of all goods than to another agent. Is there a Pareto optimal mechanism satisfying Population Monotonicity and No Domination? If the answer is yes, can we also meet Equal Split Guarantee (on top of the three first properties)?
Repeated applications of inequality (5) gives the following interpretation of the axiom: an agent never benefits when the population sharing a given cake increases.
Definition 1 (Steinhaus 1948). A mechanism satisfies Equal Split Guarantee if the welfare of any agent, at any profile, is not below that of his per capita share of the resources.
In both questions we assume arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences.

accepted.question_text: In the one-input joint-production problem with a convex production set and arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences, does there exist a Pareto optimal mechanism satisfying both the Egalitarian Lower Bound and Population Monotonicity? Here the Egalitarian Lower Bound requires each agent's final welfare to be at least that agent's unanimity welfare, namely the welfare the agent could secure from a one-nth share of the production set if all agents had that same preference, and Population Monotonicity requires that when more agents appear to share the technology, the pre-existing population does not become better off.
accepted.context_brief: Joint production under ELB and population monotonicity

evidence.quote: Question 2. Joint Production. (One input, convex production set). Is there a Pareto optimal mechanism satisfying the egalitarian lower bound and Population Monotonicity?

The second notion of fairness is the analog of Equal Split Guarantee. In a nutshell it gives to each agent a claim on his (1/n)-th share of the production set.
